subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Movement Competence: Net/Wall, Target, and Striking Categories
title: Synthesis and review: accuracy under a small amount of pressure under transfer
focus: accuracy under a small amount of pressure
essentialQuestion: How does the goal of an activity change the movement it asks for?
materials: Optional: three small household objects may represent boundaries, teammates, or targets. Sport equipment, a court, and additional players are not required.
Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
movementCues: Start balanced with eyes scanning the whole space, not fixed on one object or person.
Move or point into open space, then recover to a position that protects the next likely option.
Decide early, communicate the choice clearly, and use controlled movement with no contact required.
Pause after the pattern and explain what cue changed the decision; good positioning matters more than speed.
Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
spaceSetup: Clear a dry, non-slip area at least two arm-spans wide when available. Mark the boundary with visible household objects or imaginary lines, remove furniture, cords, pets, and breakables, and keep a stable chair or wall nearby if support helps. Low-space path: clear one arm-span while seated or standing and keep every movement in place.

optional: Optional: three small household objects may represent boundaries, teammates, or targets. Sport equipment, a court, and additional players are not required.
householdSubstitutes: Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit home option: use hand signals, floor points, or a paper diagram to show ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; then walk, wheel, gesture, or describe the pattern in a cleared area. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.

safetyRules: Check the floor, ceiling, footwear or mobility supports, boundary, and any optional item before moving. Keep people, pets, furniture, cords, and breakables outside the boundary.
Use a self-selected easy-to-moderate challenge, breathe continuously, and choose control over speed, force, distance, or repetition.
Rest, reduce range or pace, use support, or choose the non-movement planning path at any time without losing credit.
Use solo, shadow, or walk-through practice at home. No collision, guarding contact, wrestling, tackling, or movement toward another person is required.
stoppingRules: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, or any movement that feels unsafe; tell a trusted adult.
Stop when a person, pet, object, or slippery surface enters the movement area. Reset the area before continuing.
After a head impact, injury, or symptoms that do not settle with rest, do not resume the activity until a trusted adult or qualified professional says it is safe.
accessibleAdaptation: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit home option: use hand signals, floor points, or a paper diagram to show ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; then walk, wheel, gesture, or describe the pattern in a cleared area. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
activitySteps: Setup: read the equipment, space, safety, stop, and transfer-evidence rules; clear the area and choose the standard or adapted path.
Prepare: begin with comfortable joint movements or a low-intensity rehearsal of the planned evidence while breathing normally.
Practice: apply the movement cues for accuracy under a small amount of pressure at a self-selected challenge, resting or reducing the range whenever control changes.

Apply: perform, simulate, diagram, gesture, or fully describe accuracy under a small amount of pressure under the authored transfer condition and preserve every required cue, decision, comparison, or revision. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
Finish: transition to easy movement or rest, then name one safety check and one adjustment for next time. No score, measurement, photo, or recording is needed beyond the stated transfer evidence.
privacySafeScenario: Show competence in one activity from each of the three categories and explain what each demanded that the others did not.
studentTask: Learner works accuracy under a small amount of pressure in a rally, round, or innings decision sequence where a played or modelled score state creates pressure and the routine has to hold anyway at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of accuracy under a small amount of pressure degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner clears or accurately describes the safe space and selects the standard, accessible, or no-equipment path for accuracy under a small amount of pressure.

The learner performs or fully models accuracy under a small amount of pressure under the authored transfer condition and supplies the stated cue, decision, comparison, or revision evidence. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
The learner identifies the equipment choice (including none), one safety or stop rule, and one technique adjustment or next step.

A seated, supported, reduced-range, solo, low-space, no-equipment, simulated, diagrammed, or described version earns equal credit only when it preserves the same transfer evidence. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
adaptationChoices: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires the learner to show how the decision changes as the score state changes. Playing, diagramming, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit when it preserves that score-dependent decision evidence; a numeric result is not required.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of accuracy under a small amount of pressure yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

Distances, implement size, object speed, and target size are all learner-set. Seated and one-handed versions of every activity are provided, and a learner may substitute a self-designed activity that meets the same category description.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where accuracy under a small amount of pressure shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
